text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of code without changing how it works. Think of it as cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the room still serves the same purpose, but it becomes easier to use and more pleasant to live in. In programming, this means renaming confusing variables, breaking large functions into smaller ones, or removing duplicate code. The main goal is to enhance readability, making it simpler for other developers (or your future self) to understand and modify. When code is hard to follow, it often accumulates "technical debt"—a kind of hidden cost that slows down future changes. Regular refactoring pays off this debt, keeping the project healthy and agile. Though it takes time upfront, the long-term benefits of clearer, more maintainable software are well worth the effort.
